Australian Army PFA

Australian Army pre-entry fitness assessment

ENTRY FITNESS TEST

At a glance

These are Australian Army general-entry combat and officer-entry pre-entry standards. Non-combat roles and other services use separate requirements.

FEATURED ACTIVITYShuttle runLevel 7.5 for combat / officer entry

What the test includes

  • Sit-ups (feet held) — 45
  • Push-ups — Women 8; men 15
  • Shuttle run — Level 7.5

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

These are Australian Army general-entry combat and officer-entry pre-entry standards. Non-combat roles and other services use separate requirements.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

ActivityPublished requirementHow it works
Sit-ups (feet held)45Follow the published secured-feet technique.
Push-upsWomen 8; men 15Count accepted repetitions using the applicable official technique.
Shuttle runLevel 7.5Use the specified recording and shuttle instructions.

Scoring and scope

The PFA is an entry assessment, not a complete selection or serving-member standard. Follow the current role-specific criteria and demonstrations.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Build strict push-ups using an easier variant if necessary.
  • Train controlled trunk endurance with rest between sessions.
  • Combine easy running with a few measured shuttle turns before attempting a full test.

Putting it into a training week

Choose two or three repeatable sessions addressing the listed movements and aerobic demand. Leave recovery between harder efforts; record comparable results rather than testing maximally every week.

Common mistakes

  • Using Air Force or Navy thresholds for Army combat entry.
  • Mixing secured and unsecured sit-up counts or different shuttle recordings.

What to log

Record role, valid push-ups, secured sit-ups and last accepted shuttle level.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.
